title: Per-tenant KV residency, soft-eviction arbitration, and prefill prioritization for paged-attention
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: On multi-tenant paged-attention workloads we see two correlated failure modes: (1) fragmentation of KV slots across tenants and sequence lengths leads to poor slot utilization and frequent evictions that thrash serving kernels; (2) aggressive prefill behavior for long-running requests stalls decode waves and causes p99+ latency spikes for latency-sensitive tenants. These issues compound when kernel selection favors bulk-prefill fused kernels that assume steady KV residency, leading to bursts of kernel reconfiguration and increased per-token latency.

Goal: Implement a tenant-aware residency allocator with soft-eviction arbitration and a prefill prioritization layer that cooperates with kernel selection policies. This should reduce cross-tenant interference, lower eviction churn, and preserve tail latency for high-priority tenants while keeping overall throughput high.

High-level approach:
1) Residency buckets: Allocate KV memory into lightweight per-tenant "residency buckets" by estimated working set (hot / warm / cold). Buckets are sized dynamically using an occupancy estimator computed from recent hit rates and token arrival distributions. This prevents a single tenant with a large cold tail from monopolizing contiguous KV pages.
2) Soft-eviction arbitration: Eviction becomes a two-step process: mark-and-signal then reclaim. When memory pressure occurs, candidates are scored by a residency score that includes tenant priority, last-use timestamp, fragment compactability, and estimated re-prefill cost. Marked pages are signalled to a background compactor which attempts contiguous coalescing before final reclaim. This reduces fragmentation and avoids immediate decode stalls.
3) Prefill prioritization queue: Requests are classified into priority classes (latency-sensitive, throughput-batch, background rebuild). Prefill work is scheduled with a short-term arbitration window that reserves a small hotset for latency-sensitive classes. For throughput/batch classes we allow deferred prefill or opportunistic prefill during idle cycles. Prefill tasks expose hints to kernel-selection (e.g., prefer low-latency tiled kernel for high-priority short prefill).
4) Kernel co-scheduling signals: Extend kernel selection API to accept runtime hints (prefill vs decode, priority class) so the dispatcher can choose kernels optimized for the expected access pattern (fused prefill kernels for contiguous cold loads; tiled/streaming kernels for latency-bound decode).

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict per-tenant hard quotas reduce interference but hurt utilization for bursty tenants. We favor soft-residency with eviction arbitration to avoid global underutilization.
- Background compaction introduces CPU/GPU overhead and must be rate-limited; we choose adaptive compaction based on reclaimed fragmentation and tail-latency budget.
- Kernel hinting increases complexity in the matchmaking layer; we will keep hinting optional and fall back to existing heuristics when absent.

Expected benefits:
- Reduced eviction churn and KV re-prefill for top 10% heavy tenants (target 30-50% lower eviction rate).
- Lower p99/p995 token latency for latency-sensitive tenants (target 15-25% improvement).
- Improved overall GPU utilization by reducing wasted fragmented pages and enabling larger contiguous prefill batches in background windows.

Risks:
- Misclassification of request priority could starve throughput jobs. Mitigation: dynamic time-sharing and decay of reservation for hotset.
- Background compaction could increase jitter. Mitigation: rate-limits, backoff tied to SLO signals.

Open questions:
- Exact scoring weights for residency score (tenant-priority vs fragment-size vs last_access). Propose an A/B sweep in staging.
- How much hotset to reserve per tenant by default. Proposal: start with 5% of pool pinned across tenants then adjust by usage.

Deliverables: design doc, allocator implementation, kernel hinting extension, prefill scheduler, unit+integration tests, microbench harness, staging rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: New allocator exposes per-tenant residency buckets configurable via runtime flags
Eviction flow marks candidates and background compactor can coalesce at least 60% of marked fragments under typical workloads
Prefill prioritization reduces prefill-induced decode stalls on benchmark SLO-set by >=15% p99 improvement
Kernel hinting accepted by dispatcher and observed switching cost < 2% throughput regression on mixed workloads
End-to-end performance dashboard (per-tenant hit rate, eviction rate, prefill-cancel rate, decode p99) populated for rollout
implementation_steps: 1. Write design doc and review with Runtime and Serving teams (Link in attachments)
2. Add residency-bucket metadata to KV allocator and expose flags for bucket sizes
3. Implement eviction scoring and mark-and-signal protocol
4. Add background compactor worker with rate-limits and compaction heuristics
5. Implement prefill prioritization queue and API for request class hints
6. Add kernel hinting API and dispatcher plumbing to accept prefill/decode hints
8. Unit tests -> microbench harness -> staging cluster perf tests
9. Canary rollout behind feature flag; monitor and iterate
test_plan: Unit tests for eviction scoring and bucket assignment
Synthetic microbench: multi-tenant mix with heavy cold tails to measure eviction churn
Staging perf: run 24h job with mixed latency-sensitive and throughput tenants; measure p50/p95/p99/p995 tokens/ms
A/B sweep of residency scoring weights to find stable default
Failover test: simulate compactor worker crash and ensure safe fallback reclaim path
Load test for kernel hinting path to ensure dispatcher fallbacks keep throughput stable
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime-1.22 flag: kv_residency_v2 + prefill_arbitration
Canary on 5% internal tenants for 48h; validate metrics and alerts
Expand to 25% with automated rollback if p99 increases > 10% or eviction rate regressions > 30%
Full fleet ramp pending 7-day stability window and dashboard green
Post-rollout: monitor for 30 days and run automated scoring recalibration weekly
